claim: At the rates of the week of 2026-09-24 (30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%), a $320,000 15-year loan costs $2,773.49 a month. Paying the 30-year loan off in the same 15 years takes $2,881.62 a month: $108.13 more each month and $19,464 more over 15 years. Paying only the 15-year payment on the 30-year loan finishes in 192.9 months, about a year late. The 30-year loan's required payment is $2,135.42, so that $19,464 is the price of being allowed to drop to the lower payment. Across 1,831 weeks since August 1991 the 30-year rate was 0.2 to 1.0 point above the 15-year (mean 0.57; at least half a point in 62.9% of weeks), and the same extra cost ranged from $6,097 to $29,502 (median $16,594). History, not a forecast.

assumptions: Loan $320,000, fixed rate, level monthly payments, no points, fees, taxes, insurance or escrow.
The weekly survey averages stand for the rates a typical borrower would be offered on each term in the same week.
Paying the 30-year loan 'on a 15-year schedule' means a level payment that retires it in exactly 180 months at the 30-year rate.
No discounting, no investment of payment differences, no tax effects.
